CONFIDENCE: 0.28  
EXPLANATION:  
The spectrum is dominated by the classical “acetophenone fingerprint”:  
• very strong 1001 cm⁻¹ ring-breathing band of a monosubstituted / para-substituted benzene;  
• 1302 cm⁻¹ intense CH₃ twisting/umbrella vibration of an acetyl group;  
• 1580 cm⁻¹ aromatic C=C stretch;  
• 1665 cm⁻¹ strong conjugated C=O stretch typical of an acetyl group directly attached to an aromatic ring.  

We also observe medium bands at 1171, 1458 and 536 cm⁻¹ that match CH bending and ring deformations reported for hydroxy-acetophenones.  
The spectrum lacks an intense N–H stretch near 3300 cm⁻¹ that would be expected for an aniline (candidate 2) and shows no features characteristic of additional hetero-cycles or multiple C=O groups present in candidates 3–10.  
Among the molecules that contain a single acetyl group on a benzene ring, candidate 1 (p-hydroxy-acetophenone, CC(=O)c1cccc(O)c1) best accounts for the observed strong acetyl and phenolic benzene pattern, making it the most plausible assignment.
